rules.heading: Put only what Claude would get wrong without it in the root file
rules.nativeFeature: CLAUDE.md writing guidance, /doctor checkup trims, CLAUDE.md length warning
rules.evidence: Native best-practices already asks 'Would removing this cause Claude to make mistakes?' and /doctor proposes cutting derivable content, but the length warning only warns and nothing fails a long file; the rule names that floor and adds a checker ratchet plus a read-first and conflict-winner opening the harness lacks (it has no override semantics across files).
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md#write-an-effective-claude-md ; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (My CLAUDE.md is too large; How CLAUDE.md files load)

rules.heading: Keep the auto-memory index to hooks, and hold it under its cap
rules.nativeFeature: MEMORY.md load limit and length reminder/error
rules.evidence: The harness reminds Claude near the MEMORY.md limit and returns an error past it on Claude's own writes only, while the rule treats that as the floor and adds a checker that also catches hand edits, overlong cue lines, and fact-loss on trim.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (How it works; MEMORY.md length reminder and error)

rules.heading: Give a domain rule a paths list, and never leave a rule file unscoped
rules.nativeFeature: Path-scoped rules (paths frontmatter), InstructionsLoaded hook, /context
rules.evidence: Native path-scoped rules load on file access and are summarized away at compaction, while unparseable frontmatter silently loads the rule as unscoped; the rule adds a posture (scope everything) and drift/coload checks, but its 'confirm the scoping defers loading' step names no native way to confirm it.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Path-specific rules; Rule frontmatter reference); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (InstructionsLoaded); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window.md#what-survives-compaction
rules.proposedWording: Confirm the scoping defers loading before you count on it, with `/context` or the InstructionsLoaded hook's load reason, since frontmatter that does not parse loads the rule as if unscoped; tell the reader to grep the rules directory when no matching file is open.

rules.heading: Make a procedure a skill, not a rule
rules.nativeFeature: Skills (on-demand body, always-on description), memory docs guidance to move procedures into skills, claude plugin eval and skill-creator evals
rules.evidence: Native docs say multi-step procedures belong in a skill or path-scoped rule and stop there; the rule says so explicitly and adds what a skill then owes (one-sentence description, hazards section, edit-timing note, evals first) plus a length cap that forces the move.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (When to add to CLAUDE.md; Write effective instructions); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md

rules.heading: Keep a skill body short, its references one level deep, and its name equal to its directory
rules.nativeFeature: Skill frontmatter name, SKILL.md length guidance, skill listing description cap, plugin skill namespacing
rules.evidence: The docs say a skill's `name` frontmatter is the command name (defaulting to the directory) and the under-500-lines figure is advisory guidance, so the rule's claim that a personal or project skill's name is only a display label invoked by directory, and its calling the length a 'documented ceiling', contradict the documented behavior even though the name-equals-directory check itself is a sound complement.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/slash-commands.md and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md (Frontmatter: name; SKILL.md length guidance); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components#skills
rules.proposedWording: Hold the body under the length Claude Code's docs recommend, or a lower cap you configure, and move detail into references rather than appending. The harness takes a skill's command from its `name` field, defaulting to the directory, and a plugin skill's `name` replaces only the last segment of its namespaced command, so holding the name equal to the directory keeps the command and the path the same everywhere.

rules.heading: Disable model invocation on a skill with side effects
rules.nativeFeature: disable-model-invocation frontmatter
rules.evidence: Native docs already recommend `disable-model-invocation: true` for side-effect workflows and the flag blocks Claude's own invocation, but nothing decides which effects count or gates later phases; the rule names the native block and adds those postures.

rules.heading: Set the model explicitly on every subagent and workflow agent
rules.nativeFeature: Subagent model resolution order, CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, per-invocation effort, availableModels substitution, cost guidance on model choice
rules.evidence: The harness resolves an omitted model to the env var and then the session model, and its cost guidance (Sonnet for most work, Haiku for simple subagents, Opus for complex reasoning) is advisory only; the rule turns that into an explicit per-call posture, a pinned roster, a budget ceiling, and an eval anchor.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md (Model resolution); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/model-config.md (Subagent model; Restricting models); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs.md (Choose the right model)

rules.heading: Make a must-hold rule a hook, fail it closed, and test it with real payloads
rules.nativeFeature: PreToolUse hooks, exit code 2, onFailure: block, PermissionRequest decision object, hook `if` field, deny rule precedence
rules.evidence: The rule correctly sets onFailure block as the floor and keeps decisions out of the best-effort `if` filter, but its clause 'only the pre-tool event reads a failing exit as a block' overstates: the docs list exit 2 as blocking on many events (UserPromptSubmit, Stop, PostToolBatch and others), with PermissionRequest among those that ignore it.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Exit code semantics; onFailure; PermissionRequest hook; Hook if field)
rules.proposedWording: Know where that exit stops binding: among the events that gate a tool call, a blocking exit stops the call at the pre-tool event, while the permission-request event ignores it and runs on, so a guard there has to deny through its decision object instead.

rules.heading: Run adversarial review in a fresh subagent with a named lens
rules.nativeFeature: /code-review bundled skill, best-practices adversarial review step, forks inherit conversation, checkpoint limits for subagent edits
rules.evidence: Native /code-review already reviews the diff in a fresh subagent and the docs advise telling the reviewer to flag only correctness and requirement gaps; the rule starts there and adds a named lens, risk-matched refuters, a must-fix definition, and a round-stopping verdict.

rules.heading: Plan when the approach is uncertain, and clear the context after two failed corrections
rules.nativeFeature: Best-practices: explore, plan, then code; common failure patterns (correcting over and over)
rules.evidence: Native best-practices already says to plan when uncertain or multi-file, to skip the plan when the diff fits in one sentence, and to /clear after repeated failed corrections, with the same advisory enforcement, so only the re-read-the-ruling line adds anything.
rules.proposedWording: Follow Claude Code's best-practices guidance on planning only when the approach is uncertain and on clearing the context after repeated failed corrections; add the step it lacks and re-read the source of a ruling immediately before you act on it, since a ruling can land mid-session.

rules.heading: Keep a session to one task, and start fresh rather than resume a large idle one
rules.nativeFeature: Prompt caching TTL and compaction cost, native resume warning, SessionStart cache fields, /usage prompt-cache line, idle compaction
rules.evidence: The docs explain the cache rewrite after an idle gap and advise /clear and compacting at natural breaks, and SessionStart exposes estimated_cache_write_usd; the rule names the native resume warning as floor and adds dollar-based warnings for API and cloud billing plus a held first prompt the harness lacks.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching.md (Compacting the conversation; Cache lifetime; Check cache performance); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (SessionStart hook)

rules.heading: Treat git state as shared across sessions
rules.nativeFeature: --worktree / EnterWorktree, worktree.baseRef, .worktreeinclude, worktree isolation enforcement
rules.evidence: Native worktrees enforce isolation once a session is inside one but never require entering one or forbid branching in the main checkout; the rule prefers the native tool for its defaults and adds that posture with a pre-tool branch guard.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (Ask Claude to create a worktree; How Claude Code enforces isolation; Manage worktrees manually)

rules.heading: Keep the committed settings narrow and the local settings local
rules.nativeFeature: Permission rules and scope merging, workspace trust for project allow rules, settings.local.json auto-exclude, MCP rule syntax, auto mode suspension of broad allows, sandbox
rules.evidence: The harness merges allow lists across scopes, gates project allows on trust, auto-excludes settings.local.json, and documents Bash rules as not a security boundary; the rule builds a narrow-allow, escape-hatch-deny posture and a config check on top of those primitives.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Permission rule evaluation order; Bash rule matching; Workspace trust; WebFetch, MCP, Agent, Cd and parameter rules); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/settings (Settings precedence and merging)

rules.heading: Read a resume file as a harness artifact, not a handoff
rules.nativeFeature: Checkpointing and session transcripts
rules.evidence: The docs describe checkpoints as session-level recovery that is not a replacement for version control, which matches the rule's stance that a harness-written resume record is not a handoff protocol; the rule adds the handoff skill as the real artifact.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing.md (Relation to git / version control); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md (Where transcripts are stored)

rules.heading: Hand off through the repo, not a standing issue
rules.nativeFeature: Auto memory
rules.evidence: Auto memory is machine-local but is loaded every session and shared across worktrees of the same repo, so the rule's claim that it is 'never shared' and 'cannot be the channel the next session reads' overstates; what holds is that it is machine-local, absent from subagents and cloud sessions, and outside review.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Auto memory storage location and sharing; Auto memory and subagents)
rules.proposedWording: Auto memory is the harness's own place for ongoing work, but it is machine-local, unseen by subagents and cloud sessions, and never reviewed, so a handoff cannot rely on it as the channel the next session reads.

rules.heading: Check for a peer session before driving shared external state
rules.nativeFeature: ListAgents and SendMessage cross-session messaging; agent messages carry no approval authority
rules.evidence: The harness already denies agent messages the power to approve permission prompts or change permissions, and the rule extends that to spend, merges, and external writes, adding peer checks, a single-writer baton, and worker naming the harness does not provide.

notes:
I classified 16 headings and skipped "Don't", as instructed. The rule file is <repo>/plugins/house/modules/claude-code/rules/claude-code.md.

Rules I was unsure about:

1. "Keep a skill body short..." I marked this CONFLICT because I applied the definition strictly. The name-equals-directory check itself is a sound complement. Only the explanatory clause contradicts the facts: the skill docs say `name` is the command name and defaults to the directory, but the rule says the harness treats it as a display label and invokes by directory. "Documented ceiling" also overstates what the docs treat as advisory guidance. If the house author has observed the display-label behavior in practice, the facts here do not show it, so it should be re-verified before the reword lands.

2. "Set the model explicitly..." This rule refers to a "workflow model variable" that, once set, replaces every workflow agent's model. The facts document no such variable. They only say CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL covers workflow agents at lower precedence than a script-named model, and that CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE overrides frontmatter and call models. The clause is either about a variable outside the gathered docs or it is wrong. I left the rule as keep but flag the clause for verification. The rule's "Opus is moderately priced" rationale does not appear in the cost docs either, which only say to reserve Opus for complex reasoning.

3. "Make a must-hold rule a hook..." I used COMPLEMENT plus a reword rather than CONFLICT, because the inaccurate clause ("only the pre-tool event" honors a blocking exit) does not change what the rule tells anyone to do. Separately, "only a pre-tool hook stops the action" ignores that deny rules also stop actions. The next sentence covers this, so I left it alone.

4. "Keep the committed settings narrow..." The clause saying a parameter-scoped rule on a server tool is dropped by the loader is only partly backed. The facts confirm that allow rules with parentheses on `mcp__` tools are skipped, and that parameter rules on primary content fields are ignored. They also describe Tool(param:value) deny and ask rules as working in general. So "drops it" may be true only for allow rules. The claims that the agent listing labels a print-mode run interactive, and that bare mode keeps a worker out of the listing ("Check for a peer session..."), are not in the facts either. I kept both rules because nothing contradicts them outright.

5. "Read a resume file..." No fact describes a harness-written checkpoint or resume file carrying a session id, snapshot ref, and resume command. Checkpoints and transcripts are internal stores. The rule may describe an older or undocumented artifact. If it no longer exists, the rule is closer to UNIQUE or obsolete.

6. "Plan when the approach is uncertain..." I marked this DUPLICATE: its first two lines restate best-practices guidance almost verbatim, with the same advisory enforcement. I proposed citing that guidance as the floor rather than deleting it, because the re-read-the-ruling line adds something.

7. "Disable model invocation..." The point that a print-mode run still expands a named skill is not in the facts. Native best-practices already recommends the flag for side-effect skills, so the first sentence is near-duplicate. The phase-gate posture is what makes it a complement.

rules.heading: Anchor every claim to a grep-able token
rules.nativeFeature: /doctor prompt-audit (flags references to files or commands that don't exist)
rules.evidence: The prompt audit checks only instruction files, only on demand, and only proposes edits (memory.md#audit-your-instruction-files), while this rule gates every backticked token in every scanned doc on every commit.
rules.proposedWording: The harness's prompt audit flags a missing file or command only in instruction files and only when someone runs it; this gate resolves every backticked token in every scanned doc on every commit.

rules.heading: Run the docs gate before pushing and in the build
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No fact describes a native docs check that runs before push or in CI; the GitHub Action and Code Review run Claude on PRs but never gate on doc tokens, and Code Review never blocks a merge (code-review.md).

rules.heading: Give every rule file a paths list whose first segment resolves
rules.nativeFeature: Path-scoped rules (paths frontmatter); compaction survival of unscoped rules
rules.evidence: Native rules with no paths load at launch at .claude/CLAUDE.md priority, unparseable frontmatter loads as unscoped, and a glob that matches nothing just never fires (memory.md Path-specific rules), so the rule's check is enforcement the harness does not have, and it already cites that floor accurately.

rules.heading: Put a fact where its litmus test says it belongs
rules.nativeFeature: CLAUDE.md writing guidance (route multi-step or single-area content to skills or path-scoped rules) and /doctor checkup trims of codebase-derivable content
rules.evidence: Native guidance routes instruction-file content between CLAUDE.md, skills and path-scoped rules and says to exclude what the code already shows (memory.md; best-practices.md#write-an-effective-claude-md), but it does not cover the README, changelog, archive, or the documentation modes this rule adds.
rules.proposedWording: The harness's guidance routes instruction content between the root file, skills, and path-scoped rules and has its checkup cut what the code already says; this rule carries that routing to every document the repo keeps.

rules.heading: State a rule as imperative, why, anchor, receipts
rules.nativeFeature: CLAUDE.md writing guidance (concrete, verifiable, structured) and /doctor prompt-audit
rules.evidence: The documented prompt audit looks for older-model wording, missing files or commands, and contradictions, and the docs name no other patterns (memory.md#audit-your-instruction-files), so the claim that it judges a prohibition by provenance and an instruction by its enforcement is not supported by the facts.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Audit your instruction files; Write effective instructions)
rules.proposedWording: The harness asks for concrete, verifiable instructions, and its prompt audit, when run, checks for stale wording, missing references, and contradictions; the why and the Anchor line show each rule's provenance and enforcement to that audit and to a human reviewer. Keep each `## Don't` line the negative of a rule above, so it inherits that rule's reason instead of reading as a bare ban.

rules.heading: Move dates, names, and measured numbers out of rule prose
rules.nativeFeature: Best-practices CLAUDE.md exclusions (frequently changing info) and /doctor prompt-audit
rules.evidence: The docs advise keeping frequently changing information out of CLAUDE.md and describe the audit as flagging only older-model instructions, missing references and contradictions (best-practices.md; memory.md), so the claim that it flags volatile specifics and one-session lessons is not in the facts.
rules.proposedWording: The harness's guidance keeps frequently changing information out of instruction files, and its prompt audit flags instructions written for older models only when run and only as a proposal; the shape check makes the volatile-specifics test a gate on every commit.

rules.heading: Keep files under budget, and raise a ceiling only with a written reason
rules.nativeFeature: CLAUDE.md size guidance and warnings (recommended length, combined limit, hard size skip)
rules.evidence: The harness only warns at startup and in /status, skips only past a hard size cap, and says longer files 'consume more context and reduce adherence' (memory.md), so the ratchet adds enforcement and wider scope, but the rule misquotes the docs as 'may reduce adherence'.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Write effective instructions; My CLAUDE.md is too large)
rules.proposedWording: The Claude Code docs set a recommended line target per instruction file because longer files consume more context and reduce adherence, and every loaded line costs context on each read.

rules.heading: Cut, don't append, and trim on a fixed cadence
rules.nativeFeature: /doctor checkup trims for CLAUDE.md; periodic-review writing guidance
rules.evidence: The checkup only proposes trims for a checked-in CLAUDE.md and the docs only advise periodic review (memory.md), which the rule cites correctly, but no fact supports attributing 'an empty diff beats a manufactured one' to the harness's audit.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (My CLAUDE.md is too large; Write effective instructions); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices.md#avoid-common-failure-patterns
rules.proposedWording: A pass that finds no candidate cuts nothing, since an empty diff beats a manufactured one, and the prompt to look is what does the work.

rules.heading: Split a file only when splitting narrows what loads
rules.nativeFeature: @path imports, unscoped rules, path-scoped rules, nested CLAUDE.md lazy loading, skills
rules.evidence: The docs say imports load at launch and so organize without cutting context cost, and unscoped rules load at launch, while path-scoped rules, nested files and skills load on demand (memory.md); the rule cites this accurately and adds the co-load cap.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Import additional files; Organize rules with .claude/rules/; How CLAUDE.md files load)

rules.heading: Opt a point-in-time doc out with a file-level reason
rules.nativeFeature: Block-level HTML comments stripped from CLAUDE.md
rules.evidence: The rule's claim matches the docs: block-level HTML comments are stripped from CLAUDE.md before injection but kept in code blocks and visible through the Read tool (memory.md); the archive opt-out and drift scan have no native counterpart.

rules.heading: Don't document a command that does not exist
rules.nativeFeature: /doctor prompt-audit (references to files or commands that don't exist)
rules.evidence: The audit flags missing files or commands only in instruction files and only on demand (memory.md#audit-your-instruction-files); the rule says so accurately and extends the check to the README, changelog and every scanned doc on every commit.

rules.heading: Ship the docs and changelog edit in the same PR as the change
rules.nativeFeature: Code Review managed service (reads CLAUDE.md, flags violations, never blocks)
rules.evidence: Code Review flags CLAUDE.md violations, marks minor issues as non-blocking Nits and 'never approves or blocks the pull request', on Team and Enterprise only (code-review.md), but no fact says it flags outdated documents as such, so the rule should cite the documented behavior.
rules.proposedWording: The hosted Code Review service, where it runs, flags violations of the repo's CLAUDE.md but never blocks a merge, so the template's binary is what holds it.

notes:
I classified all 12 rules: 11 complement the harness and 1 is unique. None duplicates or conflicts with native behavior. Six keep their wording; six need a reword. Four of the rewords fix claims about the harness that the supplied facts don't support:

- **"State a rule as imperative, why, anchor, receipts"** says the prompt audit judges a prohibition by its provenance and an instruction by what enforces it.
- **"Move dates, names, and measured numbers out of rule prose"** says the audit flags volatile specifics and one-session lessons.
- **"Cut, don't append, and trim on a fixed cadence"** attributes "an empty diff beats a manufactured one" to the audit.
- **"Ship the docs and changelog edit in the same PR as the change"** says a hosted reviewer may flag an outdated document. The facts only show Code Review flagging CLAUDE.md violations.

The facts say the audit looks for three things: instructions written for older models, references to missing files or commands, and files that contradict each other. They also say the docs list no other patterns. Those three claims may come from the audit's own prompt or from an earlier research pass in the harness research bank, which I was told not to use. If that research confirms them, the rewords for those three rules can be dropped. These are the rules I'm least sure about.

**"Keep files under budget, and raise a ceiling only with a written reason"** quotes the docs as saying "may reduce adherence". The docs say "reduce adherence". The rule also states the line count as a number, which its sibling rule on measured numbers in prose forbids unless it is a pinned figure.

**"Give every rule file a paths list whose first segment resolves"** sends must-hold rules to the root file. The context-window page also allows dropping the paths frontmatter so a rule is re-injected after compaction. House chooses not to allow unscoped rule files, which is a stricter posture, not a conflict, so I kept the wording. It may be worth saying the native alternative is closed on purpose.

**"Run the docs gate before pushing and in the build"** is unique: no fact shows a native docs gate before push or in CI.

**"Opt a point-in-time doc out with a file-level reason"**: the facts cover HTML-comment stripping for CLAUDE.md files only, and the rule's wording matches that scope.

rules.heading: Build the simplest thing that answers the question
rules.nativeFeature: Bundled /code-review skill and the Code Review service (post-diff review)
rules.evidence: The harness reviews only an existing diff, and its stated default focus is correctness ('bugs that would break production, not formatting preferences'), so nothing native steers toward least machinery before code is written (code-review.md; best-practices.md#add-an-adversarial-review-step). The current Anchor says native review flags reuse and simplification, which the facts do not support.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: none (because "simplest" is a design call); the harness's review tools (/code-review and the Code Review service) judge a diff only after it exists and focus on correctness, so reaching for the least machinery up front is this repo's requirement

rules.heading: Keep one implementation per computation, and let the gate and the report share it
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No harness fact covers making a build gate and a published report share one computation or deriving types from a schema; the native mechanisms are about context, permissions and review, not project build integrity.

rules.heading: Prove a check can fail before trusting that it passed
rules.nativeFeature: claude plugin eval no-plugin baseline (ablation) arm; Anthropic eval guidance on testing both should-occur and should-not-occur cases
rules.evidence: The eval runner's baseline arm only shows whether the plugin changed a score ('If a case scores 1.0 both with and without the plugin, the plugin isn't what made it pass') and Anthropic's guidance is advisory, so a required paired positive and negative control per check adds enforcement the harness lacks; the Anchor already names the baseline arm.

rules.heading: Verify the served artifact, not the source
rules.nativeFeature: Bundled /verify and /run skills; best-practices 'give Claude a way to verify its work'
rules.evidence: /verify builds and runs the app to confirm a change only when invoked and is advisory, and best-practices only recommends giving Claude a check, so a postbuild check that reads emitted bytes and asserts new present and prior absent adds a mechanical gate; the Anchor does not name the native floor.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: a `postbuild` check reading the emitted bytes, eval case `verify-served-artifact`; the bundled /verify runs the app only when asked and asserts nothing about the shipped bytes, so the byte-level check is this repo's requirement

rules.heading: Validate the body before writing it, because a status code is not a content check
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No harness fact describes validating fetched payloads before writing them to disk or ledgers; WebFetch summarization and the domain safety check concern Claude's own tool, not the project's fetch path.

rules.heading: Assert an invariant where its state is created, with a why and a remedy
rules.nativeFeature: CLAUDE.md is context, not enforced configuration; hooks as the deterministic layer
rules.evidence: The docs state CLAUDE.md is 'context, not enforced configuration' and that must-hold rules belong in hooks, and native cost signals such as the workflow 'Large workflow' warning are advisory, so asserting invariants (cost included) in code at the point of state creation adds enforcement; the Anchor already cites the context-not-enforcement floor.

rules.heading: Make every waiver print its reason, and give an integrity gate none
rules.nativeFeature: PreToolUse hook deny / exit 2 (holds even in bypassPermissions); onFailure: block
rules.evidence: A PreToolUse deny 'blocks even in bypassPermissions' but the harness has no notion of a reasoned, one-run waiver, so the printed reason and one-run scope are additive; the Anchor already cites the native floor accurately.

rules.heading: Read a missing field as missing, because absence is not confidence
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No native mechanism enforces distinguishing false from absent in project reporting; the harness itself follows the same principle in Code Review's severity line ('a missing line means no verdict, not zero findings'), which is consistent rather than overlapping.

rules.heading: Demote a gate that has been wrong before
rules.nativeFeature: Code Review service and /code-review report findings without blocking
rules.evidence: Native Code Review 'never approves or blocks the pull request' and its severity is advisory, so it carries no false-positive record; keeping a tally inside a checker and demoting its verdict adds posture the harness lacks, and the Anchor already says so.

rules.heading: Record a significant decision as a numbered, immutable record
rules.nativeFeature: Auto memory (machine-local, rewritable topic files)
rules.evidence: Auto memory is machine-local, 'not shared across machines', and files 'stay until you or Claude edit or delete them', so it cannot serve as an immutable shared decision record; the Anchor already draws this line.

rules.heading: Land a build-time guard with the code it protects
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: Build-time prebuild/postbuild guards are project tooling with no native counterpart; harness hooks govern Claude's tool calls, not the project's build.

rules.heading: Search public prior art before building a tool, and record what you did not adopt
rules.nativeFeature: none (claude plugin eval baseline arm is one possible refutation test the rule mentions)
rules.evidence: No harness fact asks for a prior-art search or a recorded rejection; the eval runner's with/without arm can serve as the A/B the rule names but does not overlap the rule's core requirement.

rules.heading: Pin a framework default your output depends on, with the reason beside it
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The only native analogue is advisory eval guidance to pin --model in CI 'so a model rollout isn't mistaken for a plugin regression'; nothing native pins project framework defaults or requires a reason beside a config value.

rules.heading: Enumerate from the system of record, and fail hard on a missing member
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No harness fact covers enumerating project lists from a source of truth or dating items by first appearance in history.

rules.heading: Normalize against fixed anchors, never against the live population
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: Denominator choice for reported shares has no native counterpart; the closest fact (eval docs advising to leave partial runs out of trend charts) is a narrow, advisory comparability note.

rules.heading: Make an error message teach the fix
rules.nativeFeature: Hook exit 2 stderr / permissionDecisionReason passed to Claude
rules.evidence: The harness delivers a hook's stderr or permissionDecisionReason to Claude as the block reason but places no requirement on its usefulness, so requiring remediation text and strict CLI parsing adds quality the harness lacks; the Anchor already cites this.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Exit code semantics; PreToolUse decision control)

rules.heading: Read config from the environment, and keep build, release, and run separate
rules.nativeFeature: Sandbox filesystem defaults and sandbox.credentials; auto mode classifier block on secrets entering a commit
rules.evidence: Sandboxed commands can read credential files and 'inherit Claude Code's environment, including secrets' unless sandbox.credentials denies them, and auto mode's block on 'secrets entering commit' is a classifier judgment active only in auto mode, so keeping every secret out of the repo is additive; the Anchor names the sandbox but not the classifier floor.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: the config module throws at startup on a missing key, and `.env.example` lists every key; the sandbox reads local credential files by default and the auto mode classifier's block on a secret entering a commit is a judgment call, so keeping every secret in the environment and out of the repo is this repo's requirement

notes: Unsure items: (1) "Build the simplest thing": the current Anchor says native code review "only flags reuse and simplification after the code exists"; the supplied facts describe /code-review and the Code Review service as correctness-focused and do not cover the /simplify skill, so I reworded it to what the facts support. If /simplify is a fact the owner wants cited, add it after it is verified. (2) "Land a build-time guard": "list one line per guard in the root file" could push against the native CLAUDE.md guidance (target under 200 lines; /doctor trims content Claude can derive from the codebase). notes:
File read: <repo>/plugins/house/modules/github/rules/github.md (18 rules plus Don't, which was skipped as instructed). None is a DUPLICATE or a CONFLICT.

Two rules need rewording:
- "Budget Actions minutes" says "An agent workflow caps nothing." That reads as if the GitHub Action offers no limits at all. Its docs name a turn cap in claude_args and job timeouts as cost controls; they just aren't enforced unless set.
- "Protect the default branch at the remote" gives only the local hook floor as its reason. It should also cite the harness's own floor: auto mode allows default-branch pushes, and Code Review never blocks a merge.

Rules I was unsure about:
1. "Classify a merged branch by its PR state". Its claim that "the harness's auto-mode classifier [will] refuse an agent-side remote-branch delete" isn't shown by the facts. They name a "Git Destructive" label but don't list what it blocks. Only the cloud GitHub proxy is documented as rejecting branch deletions, and only in Anthropic-hosted cloud sessions. One worktree-reuse fact also says the harness checks whether a PR merged before resetting a reopened worktree. So the Anchor's "sweep reads only local state" holds for the sweep, but not for every harness worktree path. I kept the rule but did not verify that clause.
2. "Stage explicit paths". Claude Code's built-in git instructions (which settings can turn off via includeGitInstructions) may already tell Claude to stage specific files. The facts don't give their content, so I can't rule out a partial DUPLICATE. I classed it COMPLEMENT on the classifier and permission-matching facts.
3. "Scan the built output" and "Turn on push protection". UNIQUE vs COMPLEMENT is borderline because the security-guidance plugin is a partial neighbour. It warns on secret patterns in edits and commits, but it is optional, never blocks, and doesn't look at build output or repository settings. I chose UNIQUE.
4. "Make the PR template force a docs-check answer". The Anchor says a hosted review flags stale docs only as a non-blocking nit. The facts support that Nits don't block and that CLAUDE.md violations get flagged. They don't specifically say stale docs are flagged as nits.

rules.heading: Give the agent a check it can run before you walk away
rules.nativeFeature: Bundled /verify skill and its recorded recipe at .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md; best-practices 'give Claude a way to verify its work'
rules.evidence: Per the facts, /verify builds and runs the app 'without falling back to tests or type checks', writes its own recipe to .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md, is replaced by a repo-root skill of that name, and 'runs only when you invoke it'. A suite-chaining project skill named `verify` would therefore displace the bundled skill and collide with the recipe it writes. Nothing in the facts supports the rule's claim that the harness tells Claude to run `verify` before each commit. The core obligation, one runnable check, builds on best-practices guidance and holds up.
rules.proposedWording: When the repo ships it as a project skill, give the skill its own name rather than `verify`, because a repo-root `verify` skill replaces the bundled /verify, which builds and runs the app, writes its own recipe to that path, and runs only when invoked; making the check enforced rather than advised is claude-code.md's hook ladder.

notes:
I classified all 11 headings in <repo>/plugins/house/modules/testing/rules/testing.md and skipped "## Don't" as instructed. The result is one conflict, one reword, and nine keeps.

Rules I was unsure about:

- "Give the agent a check it can run before you walk away": I marked it CONFLICT using only the supplied facts. The facts say /verify builds and runs the app, writes its own recipe to .claude/skills/verify/SKILL.md, is replaced by a repo-root skill of the same name, and runs only when invoked. Nothing in them supports the rule's claim that "the harness then tells Claude to run it before each commit, docs-only and tests-only commits excepted". That claim may come from a release note outside the gathered facts. If so, check it against that source before rewording. If the package means to replace the bundled /verify, the alternative is declare-intentional-duplicate, with the conflict over recipe-writing still stated.

- "Test the guard itself, as its own CI step": I'm unsure whether `claude plugin test` (which runs a mod's tests) counts as a native way to check a hook. A mod is the "hooks module" component type, so the rule's flat claim that "nothing native asserts" a hook's decision looked slightly too broad. I chose a small reword over a plain keep. If command hooks alone are in scope, keep is also defensible.

- "Ship every gate with a positive control and a negative control": I chose UNIQUE over COMPLEMENT. The only counterpart in the facts is Anthropic's eval-design advice, and plugin eval init proposing prompts that should and should not trigger. Both concern evals, not a repo's gates.

- "Feed a real payload through the real wiring, and never re-implement the logic under test": the claim that a malformed decision lets the action through is the default behavior. It no longer holds when a hook sets onFailure: block. The rule already gives fail-closed authoring to claude-code.md, so I kept it unchanged.

rules.nativeFeature: Worktree isolation enforcement and subagent/background-session worktrees under .claude/worktrees/
rules.evidence: The worktrees doc says isolation blocks edits and git aimed at the main checkout but does not track what a shell command writes, and the harness has no migration or schema-ledger mechanism, so the rule's sibling-checkout sweep and ledger add coordination the native isolation lacks (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md, How Claude Code enforces isolation).

rules.nativeFeature: Checkpointing and /rewind (Bash changes not tracked; not a replacement for version control)
rules.evidence: The checkpointing doc says files changed by Bash commands are not tracked and checkpoints are not a substitute for git, which matches the Anchor's reason for a runbook backup and a pasted diff (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/checkpointing.md, Limitations).

rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: None of the surveyed areas (memory, hooks, permissions, plugins, skills, sessions, subagents, git, security, tools) cover data provenance or sync-writer column ownership.

rules.heading: Let row lifecycle decide a new table, never ownership
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The harness facts say nothing about schema normalization, row churn, or column-scoped grants, so the rule has no native counterpart.

rules.heading: Add the table registry line in the same PR as the migration
rules.nativeFeature: Code Review managed service with REVIEW.md and CLAUDE.md customization
rules.evidence: The Code Review docs say a review never approves or blocks a pull request, that REVIEW.md can pull in other root files only through @includes, and that the service is limited to Team and Enterprise. A blocking schema invariant therefore adds a gate the service lacks. The Anchor's claim that an outdated CLAUDE.md statement is flagged only as a nit does not appear in today's facts (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review.md; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/code-review-customize.md).
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: a schema invariant that fails on an unregistered table and on a stale registry line, run before any publish or deploy, because the hosted review never blocks a merge, reads a registry file only when a review instructions file includes it, and is not available on every plan.

rules.heading: Store money as integer cents and reconcile against the books
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No surveyed harness fact touches column types, currency storage, or reconciliation against external statements.

rules.heading: Give each initiative its own least-privilege role
rules.nativeFeature: Permission rules and Bash sandbox (enforced at the tool boundary only)
rules.evidence: The permissions doc says Read and Edit rules do not apply to arbitrary subprocesses such as Python or Node scripts, and the sandbox controls only hostnames and filesystem paths without looking at what is sent. That supports the rule's claim that only an in-process guard can stop a privileged script's sensitive query (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, Read/Edit rule scope; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md, Network isolation).

rules.heading: Never let a write script pick its target from a dotfile
rules.nativeFeature: Bash permission rule matching (command text only; fixed wrapper strip list that excludes direnv exec)
rules.evidence: The permissions doc says Bash rules match the whole command text, are not a security boundary, and do not strip wrappers such as direnv exec. That matches the rule's reason for reading the write target only from the exported environment (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions, Bash rule matching and wildcards).

notes:
I classified eight rules; the "## Don't" section was excluded as instructed. Most of the file covers database domain matters the harness does not address. Five rules are COMPLEMENT, because their rationale or Anchor leans on a native limit that the facts confirm. Three are UNIQUE.

I propose one reword, for "Add the table registry line in the same PR as the migration". The current Anchor says the hosted review flags an outdated CLAUDE.md statement only as a non-blocking nit. Today's facts confirm only three things: the service reads CLAUDE.md and flags violations, a review never blocks a merge, and severity is advisory. So the reword leans on the verified floor (review never blocks) instead of the nit claim. The memory index points to a harness research bank that might hold an earlier source for the nit wording, but the task forbids using it, so I left that unverified rather than call it wrong.

Uncertainties:
1. Migrations rule: its line saying background sessions get their own checkouts is only partly backed by the facts. The facts describe worktrees for subagents and for backgrounded --worktree sessions, not for every background session. I kept it because the sweep still holds wherever such checkouts exist.
2. Least-privilege role rule: the sandboxing doc also says most DB drivers cannot connect through the sandbox proxy at all. That strengthens the rule's point rather than conflicting with it, so I kept the rule.
3. Dotfile rule: the direnv claim matches the documented list of wrappers that are not stripped. I treated it as an accurate citation of the native floor.

rules.heading: Deploy manually after the merge, because a merge is not a production update
rules.nativeFeature: none (auto mode classifier default soft_deny for production deploys is adjacent only)
rules.evidence: The harness facts describe no notion of a merge versus a deploy. The only nearby mechanism is the auto mode classifier, whose built-in soft_deny defaults include production deploy (auto-mode-config). That reviews a deploy command when one is run. It cannot report that a merge has not shipped, so the rule's Anchor: none reasoning matches the docs.

rules.heading: Chain the deploy guards before building anything, and give them one named escape hatch
rules.nativeFeature: none (consistent with the GitHub Actions fact that commits pushed with the default GITHUB_TOKEN trigger no workflows)
rules.evidence: No native fact provides pre-build deploy guards, CI-tip certification, or an escape hatch. The rule's fail-closed handling of an empty check-run list rests on the documented fact that GitHub does not trigger workflows on commits made with the default GITHUB_TOKEN (github-actions troubleshooting), so it agrees with the docs and does not conflict.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/github-actions.md (Troubleshooting: CI not running on Claude's commits)

rules.heading: Migrate before deploying the code that reads the schema
rules.nativeFeature: Auto mode classifier soft_deny defaults (production deploy)
rules.evidence: The documented built-in soft_deny rules name production deploy but not a production migration, and the classifier judges each action alone, with no ordering between steps (auto-mode-config). The Anchor's claim that auto mode 'holds a production migration for review' goes beyond the facts, so it should cite what the docs actually cover.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: the ordered ship script (`npm run ship`), which runs the migration step before the deploy step and exits at the first failure by name, because the auto mode classifier's default soft blocks may hold a production deploy for review but judge each action on its own, with no notion of which step must come first.

rules.heading: Invoke a deploy only through its named script
rules.nativeFeature: Permission rules (deny evaluated before allow; Bash rule matching by command text) and PreToolUse allow not bypassing deny
rules.evidence: Docs confirm that deny rules win over any allow, including a PreToolUse hook's allow. They also confirm that Bash rules match the command text rather than the program, so sh -c or an absolute path gets past them (permissions). The Anchor already states this native floor accurately and adds the script's own guards on top.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Permission rule evaluation order; Bash rule matching and wildcards; PreToolUse hooks vs mods and rules precedence)

rules.heading: Verify the deployed URL against the built file with the cache bypassed
rules.nativeFeature: none as a provider; WebFetch is a native tool the rule must route around
rules.evidence: No native fact compares a built artifact with live output. The native WebFetch caches results for a stretch, may follow no cross-host redirect, and returns a separate model call's summary rather than the raw page (tools-reference). A cache-busted byte comparison done through WebFetch would therefore be unreliable, and the Anchor should say to use a raw fetch through Bash.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: none (because the URLs worth smoke-testing change with each release; write the fetch and diff commands inline in the runbook as a raw fetch through the shell, not the WebFetch tool, which caches results and returns a model summary instead of the served bytes, and list the markers the run must print).

rules.heading: Repoint and deploy the consumer before dropping the producer's column
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: None of the harness facts covers schema contracts, producer and consumer ordering, or column drops. The nearest is the auto mode classifier's prose rules, which judge single actions and know nothing of downstream readers (auto-mode-config).

rules.heading: Restore a backup before calling it a backup
rules.nativeFeature: none (checkpoints are session-level file snapshots, explicitly not a replacement for version control or backups)
rules.evidence: Native checkpoints cover only Claude's own file-tool edits. Their snapshots are removed by the retention sweep, and the docs call them session-level recovery rather than durable history (checkpointing). Nothing native backs up or restore-tests data stores.

notes:
Unsure about three rules.

1. "Migrate before deploying the code that reads the schema": I classed it COMPLEMENT only because its Anchor leans on auto mode. The facts list "production deploy" among the default soft_deny rules but never name migrations. So "holds a production migration for review" may be true in practice, since the classifier also blocks "unknown infrastructure", but the gathered facts do not show it. That is why I proposed rewording the Anchor rather than deleting the claim.

2. "Verify the deployed URL...": I classed it UNIQUE but still proposed a reword. The rule has no native counterpart. The risk is that an assistant uses WebFetch for the "cache-busted fetch", and WebFetch's cache and model summary would defeat the check. I could also see this as a keep, with the WebFetch caveat moved to the handbook instead.

3. "Chain the deploy guards...": I kept it as is. One edge case for the guard design: the managed Code Review check run "doesn't conclude as a failure" (it ends neutral, or skipped). A guard that requires every check run on a PR head to have passed may refuse a tip that has a neutral 'Claude Code Review' run. The docs (code-review.md) suggest treating neutral as not failing. This is a handbook or guard-script matter, not a harness conflict.

Other notes:
- The "Invoke a deploy only through its named script" Anchor already describes the native floor accurately: deny beats a hook's allow, and Bash rules match the command text. The permissions docs also suggest a PreToolUse hook or sandbox for hard enforcement, which the rule could mention, but it already names the script's guards as the real gate.
- The "## Don't" section was excluded, as instructed. Its Anchor line also says the settings deny "matches the command text rather than the program", which agrees with the permissions doc.

rules.heading: End every pipeline run with a retro of invariants, deltas, and proposals
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: None of the surveyed areas describe a native per-run invariant, delta, or proposal report for user scripts. The nearest native gates are Stop hooks and /goal, which check Claude's turn and not a data store's state (best-practices.md#give-claude-a-way-to-verify-its-work).

rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The facts cover Claude Code's own session transcripts and checkpoints. They describe no run ledger, input-hash no-op, or idempotency contract for scripts that Claude writes (sessions.md; checkpointing.md).

rules.nativeFeature: none

A script-level dry-run default adds a guard the harness lacks.

rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The managed settings that fail closed (managed-settings.md#find-entries-claude-code-dropped) govern Claude Code configuration only. No fact covers a field-level write policy registry for the user's own pipelines.

rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No harness fact covers bucket-coverage gates, header-based parsing, or extraction censuses for a script's input. The plugin eval and Code Review facts cover plugin behavior and PR diffs, not pipeline data (plugin-evals.md; code-review.md).

rules.heading: Count what the agent did, not only whether it passed
rules.nativeFeature: claude plugin eval tool_used and tool_order graders, trace target, report.html per-run detail
rules.evidence: The runner can assert a call count per tool with tool_used graders and expose the trace, but it prints no tool-call mix per arm beside the outcome measures (plugin-evals.md, Grader types; Reports). The Anchor names only this package's lack of a report and does not cite the native floor.

rules.heading: Split a score gap into its causes from the transcripts before building to close it
rules.nativeFeature: claude plugin eval report.html per-run grader explanations and judge evidence; Anthropic eval guidance on reading transcripts and broken tasks
rules.evidence: Anthropic's guidance says not to trust scores until someone reads transcripts, and that a zero pass rate usually means a broken task. report.html shows each run's grader explanations (demystifying-evals; plugin-evals.md, Reports). Splitting the gap by cause before building is not native, and the Anchor cites neither source.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: none (because estimating causes from transcripts is reading, which no checker does); the harness's report shows each run's grader explanations and Anthropic's eval guidance says to read transcripts before trusting a score, but neither splits a gap by cause, so the record proposing a build names the transcripts read and the share of the gap each cause explains, and this repo writes that record.

rules.heading: Fingerprint what two arms compare, and print every field that differs
rules.nativeFeature: claude plugin eval aggregate-result.json claudeVersion field
rules.evidence: The runner's result document already records claudeVersion, so recording the harness version is partly native. It compares nothing across reports and fingerprints no corpus or label set (plugin-evals.md, JSON result). The Anchor does not cite that floor.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: tests of this repo's own comparison code that feed it a same-count content edit, a changed label set, and a citation of two members of one group, and assert the first two are flagged and the group scores at most one; the harness's runner records its version in each result document but compares nothing across reports, so the guard and its tests are this repo's addition.

notes:
I classified all eleven rules as COMPLEMENT. None duplicates the harness or conflicts with it. Most already cite the claude plugin eval runner in their Anchor. The rewords for six rules (ratio and sample, evaluate the path, deny project allows, count what the agent did, split a score gap, fingerprint) only add the missing native floor or correct it.

rules.heading: Treat every input to the model as data, never as instructions
rules.nativeFeature: Subagent output scanning and labeling; agent messages cannot approve permissions; auto mode classifier treats relayed approval claims as untrusted; security best practices for untrusted content
rules.evidence: The harness only labels subagent reports as carrying no user authority and scans them for imitated tags, which it calls 'not a security boundary', and its untrusted-content guidance is advisory; nothing native covers fetched pages, issue bodies, or memory notes, and nothing checks what is written to memory (sub-agents.md Errors, output scanning, and fallback; agent-teams.md Permissions; security.md best practices for untrusted content).

rules.heading: Give an agent, a key, and a token only what one task needs
rules.nativeFeature: Permission rules, sandbox.credentials deny, sandbox.filesystem.denyRead, sandbox network allowedDomains, permissions.blockReadsOutsideWorkingDirectories, subagent tools allowlist
rules.evidence: By default sandboxed commands inherit the session's environment, including secrets, and can read ~/.ssh and ~/.aws; sandbox.credentials deny blocks those file reads and unsets env vars, and allowedDomains is the egress allowlist. So the rule's machine-local steps are native settings the rule should name. The posture of scoping grants per task is not native (sandboxing.md Protect credentials, Network isolation).
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing.md (Sandbox filesystem defaults; Protect credentials; Network isolation)
rules.proposedWording: Do not count on the sandbox defaults, which let commands read key and cloud-credential files and inherit the session's secrets: set sandbox.credentials deny for those paths and variables, add Read deny rules since denyRead does not stop the Read tool, keep sandbox.network.allowedDomains to the hosts the work needs, and confirm where the harness honors each setting.

rules.heading: Review a change to agent config as code, and keep a second party on every consequential action
rules.nativeFeature: Plugin trust warning and hooks running outside permissions and sandbox; protected paths; workspace trust; content-scoped permissions.ask rules; ConfigChange hooks
rules.evidence: The docs confirm plugin hooks, monitors and MCP servers run with full user permissions outside the sandbox, and the install pane shows that a hook exists but not what it runs. Auto mode's classifier allows pushes to the working repo's branches, default branch included. The second-party requirement and the review posture therefore add something; the ask-rule and protected-path floors should be cited (plugins/security; auto-mode-config Auto mode classifier defaults; permission-modes Protected paths).

rules.evidence: The harness supplies the cap mechanisms (claude_args --max-turns, workflow timeouts, --max-cost-usd), but nothing native requires setting them outside the agent's reach or keeping the record out of the agent's write access, and the anchor already points to the runner's ceiling flags (github-actions.md Best practices; plugin-evals.md Command options).

rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The only native install controls apply to a plugin's own dependencies (Node deps installed with scripts disabled and frozen versions; npm plugin install scripts never run). Nothing native governs a project's lockfile, update cooldown, dependency lookup, or install scripts (plugins/loading Node.js package dependencies).

rules.nativeFeature: none

rules.evidence: Native security reviews are on demand or advisory: /security-review runs only when asked, security-guidance never blocks writes or commits, and Code Review never blocks a PR. The docs list 'your own CI static analysis/dependency scanners' as a separate layer, which the rule supplies along with a finding lifecycle (security-guidance.md Other security tooling stack; code-review.md).

I classified all seven headings and left out "## Don't" as instructed. Three calls were less certain than the rest.

The sandbox protects most of ~/.claude from writes by sandboxed commands, and the permission system protects .claude paths. The rule's "record it cannot rewrite" posture is still not natively guaranteed.
(2) "Review a change to agent config...": the first sentence says config runs "with the full access of whoever opens the repo". That is mostly consistent with the docs. The one nuance is that interactive sessions hold back repo hooks until workspace trust is accepted, while -p and SDK runs do not. I judged this not a conflict, but the owner may want to add the trust nuance.
(3) "Give an agent, a key, and a token...": the clause "scrub the subprocess environment" maps to sandbox.credentials deny, which unsets env vars, and to CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB. The env-scrub variable appears in the facts only in passing, so I named sandbox.credentials instead. The proposed wording adds Read deny rules because the facts say denyRead does not stop the Read tool.

rules.heading: Verify each quote word for word against the cited document
rules.nativeFeature: none

Plugin eval regex graders match a pattern against one target, there are no custom-code graders (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md, Grader types), and nothing native checks that a whole quotation matches one passage of a cited document.

rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: Anthropic's eval guidance names code-based, model-based and human graders and says to read transcripts, but only as engineering-blog advice (https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents). No harness feature keeps a taxonomy of retrieval quality problems or records a detector for each class.

rules.heading: Cite a primary source for every lesson, with the quote and where it was read
rules.nativeFeature: WebFetch page summaries (WebFetch returns a separate model call's answer, not the raw page)
rules.evidence: The docs say WebFetch runs a separate model call over the page and Claude receives that answer instead of the raw page, 'lossy by design' (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/security.md, WebFetch page summaries; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference.md#webfetch-tool-behavior). So a quote taken from a WebFetch result is already a summary, which is the exact drift this rule guards against, and the rule should name that floor.

rules.heading: PreToolUse branch guard (hooks/no-direct-master.sh, hooks.json PreToolUse entry)
rules.nativeFeature: PreToolUse hook deny with onFailure block; worktree isolation enforcement; protected paths; Bash permission rules
rules.evidence: Native Bash rules are not a boundary (Bash(git push *) does not stop git -C . push), worktree isolation checks only apply while a session is isolated in a worktree, and protected-path writes to .git and git config are still allowed in bypassPermissions, while a PreToolUse deny blocks in every mode including bypass, which is the floor this hook builds on.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions (Bash rule matching and wildcards); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/worktrees.md (How Claude Code enforces isolation); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permission-modes (Protected paths); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (PreToolUse decision control, onFailure: block)
rules.proposedWording: Native floor: Claude Code refuses git aimed at the main checkout only while a session is isolated in a worktree, and its protected-path check prompts on writes to .git and git config everywhere but bypass mode; this hook adds a deny that holds in every permission mode and in the main checkout, where neither native check applies.

rules.heading: Git-hook floor and its session-start arming (hooks/arm-git-hooks.sh, vendored .githooks)
rules.nativeFeature: Auto mode classifier git trust boundary; permissions.ask/deny Bash rules
rules.evidence: The auto mode classifier by default allows pushes to the working repo's branches including the default branch, and Bash ask/deny rules match only the command prefix, so nothing native stops a local commit or push to a protected branch after git resolves the ref.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/auto-mode-config (Auto mode classifier defaults and trust boundary; permissions.ask and deny versus auto mode)

rules.heading: Session-start orchestration defaults (hooks/session-start.mjs injecting orchestration/ORCHESTRATION.md)
rules.nativeFeature: SessionStart additionalContext; subagent model resolution; subagent nesting depth; EnterWorktree; adversarial review guidance
rules.evidence: Injection rides the SessionStart additionalContext channel because a plugin CLAUDE.md is never loaded, and the model-tier text correctly restates native resolution, but the line saying built-in agents cannot spawn subagents by default contradicts the documented default of three nesting layers, which general-purpose (all subagent-available tools) can use.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md (Nesting and concurrency; Built-in subagents; Model resolution); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference#standard-layout; https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks (Universal JSON output fields, 10,000 character cap)
rules.proposedWording: Subagents report back and never spawn subagents. Roster agents cannot, since none lists the Agent tool, but the harness lets other subagents, built-in general-purpose included, nest by default, so every brief to a fork or off-roster agent forbids it under DO NOT, and a session that must rule it out sets CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_SUBAGENT_SPAWN_DEPTH so nesting is off.

rules.heading: Weekly idle-rebuild cost scan (session-start.mjs plus scripts/cost-report.mjs)
rules.nativeFeature: /usage prompt cache line; status line prompt_cache
rules.evidence: /usage reports a main-conversation prompt-cache hit ratio and likely cause of the last miss for the current session only, so a cross-session scan of idle rebuild spend adds a trend the native line does not show.

rules.heading: Resume cost warning (hooks/resume-cost.mjs, SessionStart resume|fork)
rules.nativeFeature: SessionStart resume input fields (prompt_cache_likely_expired, estimated_cache_write_usd)
rules.evidence: The hook reads the resume/fork input fields the harness provides from v2.1.251 and turns them into a user-visible systemMessage, which the facts do not show the harness doing on its own.

rules.heading: Idle cache hold (hooks/idle-cache-hold.mjs, UserPromptSubmit)
rules.nativeFeature: UserPromptSubmit block; prompt cache lifetime; idle compaction
rules.evidence: Idle compaction can compact a conversation shortly before its cache expires, after which the next prompt does not rewrite the whole pre-gap history, yet the hook estimates cost from the last assistant entry's usage and does not name that native mechanism.
rules.proposedWording: Native floor: the harness's idle compaction can already compact a conversation shortly before its cache expires; this hook covers the gap that compaction did not reach and stays silent when a compaction landed after the last assistant entry.

rules.heading: Rule-load positive control (hooks/instructions-loaded.mjs, InstructionsLoaded)
rules.nativeFeature: InstructionsLoaded hook
rules.evidence: The native event only fires for observability with no decision control, and the hook persists it to a per-repo log so house doctor can prove a path-scoped rule's glob matched, which /context does not record across sessions.

rules.heading: bootstrap skill
rules.nativeFeature: /init; claude plugin init
rules.evidence: /init generates the codebase-derived CLAUDE.md and suggests improvements to an existing one, and the skill explicitly writes only the house half and leaves the rest to /init, with disable-model-invocation for its side effects.

rules.heading: conventions skill
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The facts list /memory, /context and path-scoped rule loading but no native lookup over a rule index that answers which rule covers a topic without loading rule bodies.

rules.heading: handoff skill
rules.nativeFeature: --continue/--resume; auto memory; /recap
rules.evidence: Resume restores conversation history and auto memory is machine-local, and the skill already says it carries only the next steps and decisions another machine or person must find in the repo or its issues.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions.md (What a resumed session restores); https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Auto memory storage location and sharing)

rules.heading: revise-docs skill
rules.nativeFeature: Auto memory; CLAUDE.md writing guidance; path-scoped rules
rules.evidence: Native guidance says single-area entries belong in a path-scoped rule and that 'remember' goes to machine-local auto memory, and the skill routes the shareable half to the matching path-scoped rule file instead of appending to the root file.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (Writing guidance; Asking Claude to remember vs adding to CLAUDE.md)

rules.heading: sync skill (render/check CLI driver)
rules.nativeFeature: Plugin versions and update; plugins cannot ship rules
rules.evidence: claude plugin update refreshes only the plugin cache, and a plugin cannot place rules or CLAUDE.md into a repo's context, so propagating a new plugin version into vendored repo files needs this skill.

rules.heading: trim-memory skill
rules.nativeFeature: MEMORY.md length reminder and error; MEMORY.md load limit
rules.evidence: The harness reminds Claude to shorten MEMORY.md near its limit and drops content past it on load, and the skill triggers on that reminder with a lossless, backed-up move of whole lines rather than the merge-or-drop the reminder suggests.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (MEMORY.md length reminder and error; MEMORY.md load limit)

rules.heading: Pinned agent roster (agents/scout, researcher, builder, refuter, debugger)
rules.nativeFeature: Subagent frontmatter model/effort/tools; built-in Explore and general-purpose; /code-review
rules.evidence: Plugin agents may pin model, effort and tools, and an omitted model falls through to the session model, while built-in Explore runs on the Opus alias on subscriptions, so pinned Haiku/Sonnet roles and a no-Edit refuter add cost posture and enforcement the built-ins lack.

rules.heading: Checker family: drift
rules.nativeFeature: /doctor prompt-audit
rules.evidence: prompt-audit reports references to missing files or commands only on demand, and drift makes that class a gate on every check; its header already names the native floor.

rules.heading: Checker family: todo
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No fact describes a native check for TODO markers left in CLAUDE.md.

rules.heading: Checker family: tamper
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The harness caches and versions the plugin itself but has no notion of vendored repo files checked against a lock hash.

rules.heading: Checker family: behind
rules.nativeFeature: Plugin versions, update detection and auto-update
rules.evidence: The harness announces plugin updates and recomputes the installed version, but knows nothing of the version a repo pinned in house.json, which behind compares against the installed record.

rules.heading: Checker family: shape
rules.nativeFeature: claude plugin validate
rules.evidence: validate checks skill, agent and command frontmatter but no rule-file form, and the shape header already cites that floor.

rules.heading: Checker family: lengths
rules.nativeFeature: CLAUDE.md size guidance and warnings; MEMORY.md length reminder
rules.evidence: The harness warns on an over-length CLAUDE.md at startup and /status and measures MEMORY.md on Claude's writes, while lengths turns configured limits into a repo gate and adds a memory warning outside the session; its header names the memory floor.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (CLAUDE.md size guidance and warnings; MEMORY.md length reminder and error)

rules.heading: Checker family: coload
rules.nativeFeature: Combined-length warning at session start
rules.evidence: The harness warns when launch-loaded files pass a combined limit but does not sum path-scoped rules that co-load on one read, which coload adds and its header says.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory.md (CLAUDE.md size guidance and warnings; Path-scoped rules)

rules.heading: Checker family: manifest
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: house.json is a package-specific manifest with no native schema or validator in the facts.

rules.heading: Checker family: minutes
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The facts cover Claude-in-Actions cost controls such as --max-turns and workflow timeouts but nothing that estimates a repo's scheduled Actions minutes against a budget.

rules.heading: Checker family: guard
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: /hooks only lists configured hooks read-only, and nothing native verifies that a declared branch policy has a reachable PreToolUse guard covering Bash.

rules.heading: Checker family: workflows
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: Native security tooling (security-guidance plugin, /security-review, Code Review) is model-based or pattern warnings on edits, with no deterministic gate on workflow pinning, permissions or pull_request_target checkouts.

rules.heading: Checker family: agent-config
rules.nativeFeature: Keys that never apply from repository files; workspace trust; -p trust behavior
rules.evidence: Env values in a committed settings file still apply in -p runs and under a trusted parent, so the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL check adds real protection, but permissions.defaultMode bypassPermissions no longer takes effect from project or local settings on current clients, so that entry's stated why overstates the risk.
rules.proposedWording: Current Claude Code ignores bypassPermissions as a default mode from project settings, so this flags a setting that opens every session with no permission prompt only on older clients and misleads readers on newer ones.

rules.heading: Render and vendor step (house render writing .claude/rules/house/, INDEX, AGENTS.md block)
rules.nativeFeature: Plugins cannot ship CLAUDE.md or rules; .claude/rules/ path-scoped rules
rules.evidence: A plugin's CLAUDE.md is never loaded and plugins have no rules component, while project .claude/rules/ files load natively with paths scoping, so vendoring rules into the repo is the only way to get plugin-owned rules into context.

rules.heading: Lock file (.house/lock.json)
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: The harness keeps installed_plugins.json and a versioned cache for the plugin itself but nothing that records hashes of files a plugin wrote into a repo.

rules.heading: Deviations ledger (house.json deviations)
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: No fact describes a native record of why a repo departs from a shared convention; the closest native tools (/doctor prompt-audit, claudeMdExcludes) audit or exclude files without recording a reason.

rules.heading: Length ratchets (ratchet, ratchetRaises)
rules.nativeFeature: CLAUDE.md size guidance and warnings
rules.evidence: The harness only warns past a recommended length per file and never tightens, while the ratchet pins each rule file's ceiling and requires a recorded reason to raise it, and keeps CLAUDE.md out of the ratchet in line with the native recommendation to split instead.

rules.heading: Upstream-first sync (sync refusal exits and one-issue-per-item routing)
rules.nativeFeature: none
rules.evidence: Native /import and plugin update are one-way copies with no path for a consumer's local edit to become the package rule, and the facts describe no such contribution flow.

rules.heading: Eval cases (plugins/house/evals/*/prompt.md and graders)
rules.nativeFeature: claude plugin eval case format, graders, no-plugin baseline
rules.evidence: The cases use the native prompt.md plus graders layout and frontmatter (max_turns, timeout_seconds, allowed_tools, runs) and regex and llm graders, so the runner is native and house supplies the behavior-specific cases it does not ship.
rules.citation: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-evals.md (Case format and layout; prompt.md frontmatter fields; Grader types)

notes:
Files read: <repo>/plugins/house/hooks/{hooks.json,no-direct-master.sh header,arm-git-hooks.sh,session-start.mjs,resume-cost.mjs,idle-cache-hold.mjs,instructions-loaded.mjs headers}, every skills/*/SKILL.md (first 40 lines, plus the sync upstream-first section), agents/*.md, orchestration/ORCHESTRATION.md, payload/check.mjs (header and each family's section header), evals/branch-and-pr (prompt.md and three graders). The hooks in hooks.json beyond the guard (arming, resume-cost, idle-cache-hold, instructions-loaded, cost scan) got their own entries because hooks.json was named. The deviations ledger and the ratchets are separate entries because their native footing differs.

Where I was unsure:
- Orchestration resolve-conflict: the line "Roster and built-in agents cannot by default" spawn subagents is contradicted by the sub-agents facts: nesting goes three layers deep by default, and general-purpose has every tool available to subagents. Two more ORCHESTRATION lines are worth checking. (a) "Unset CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_SUBAGENT_MODEL ... it overrides named models": that variable is not in the facts, which say a model a workflow script names counts as the per-invocation model and beats CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL. I could neither confirm nor refute it. (b) The roster's model pins can be silently overridden by CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE, which ORCHESTRATION never mentions.
- ORCHESTRATION.md is 8,450 bytes. The hooks fact caps additionalContext at 10,000 characters; past that it becomes a file with a 2,000-character preview that Claude is not asked to read. There is headroom now, but growth would silently truncate the defaults. A check worth adding.
- resume-cost: a recent commit message (b50997f) calls the hook a complement to a native resume warning added in 2.1.304. The supplied facts describe no such warning; they show only the SessionStart resume input fields. I classified it COMPLEMENT on the facts given. If a native resume warning exists, the hook header should cite it.
- idle-cache-hold: whether it actually misprices after idle compaction is my inference from the facts. The prompt-caching idle-compaction fact plus the hook reading the last assistant entry's usage suggests it, but I did not test it.
- agent-config: the bypassPermissions entry still matters for clients before v2.1.257, so I proposed rewording its stated reason, not deleting it. The facts say nothing about enableAllProjectMcpServers, so that entry is unverified against the harness.
- revise-docs says an "official instruction-file management plugin ships a revise command". That plugin is not in the facts, so the claim is unverified.
- Eval case (branch-and-pr): a regex grader uses `match: contains`. The facts list only not_contains and "count:N" as match values, so it is unclear whether `contains` is accepted or only implied as the default. Separately, there is an internal tension, not a harness conflict: the regex and llm graders reward `git checkout -b`/`git switch -c`, but ORCHESTRATION (injected by the plugin under test) says to enter a worktree and never `git checkout -b` in the main checkout. allowed_tools [Bash, Write] also leaves EnterWorktree unavailable, so a model that follows the defaults with `git worktree add -b` misses the regex grader.
- Guard: hooks.json lists MultiEdit in the matcher. The facts say path rules for MultiEdit are never consulted, but the hook header already says a tool name the harness never sends costs nothing, so I did not flag it.
- Classifying the git-hook floor as COMPLEMENT and not UNIQUE rests only on the auto-mode fact that pushes to the default branch are allowed by default.
